page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-400s-amd is a memory-oriented server belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. The instance is built on dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC hardware clocked at 2.0 GHz, spanning two physical cores with two threads per core to provide four vCPUs. The hardware includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI. Memory capacity is set to 32.0 GB, resulting in an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage is locally bundled with a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark analysis reflects strong single-thread efficiency paired with moderate multi-core scalability. Stress-ng single-core tests place the processor in the top ten percent, reinforced by an elevated Geekbench single-core score of 2146.0 and single-threaded gzip throughput reaching 32.3 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory writes demonstrate solid throughput at 112.99 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput register in the bottom quartile, and database transaction benchmarks indicate lower relative throughput compared to higher-core instances. Natural language model inference shows average throughput for smaller 135M parameter models but falls off significantly when running 7B parameter architectures on CPU.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers distinct resource efficiency for processes constrained by RAM volume rather than sheer thread concurrency. While raw parallel throughput is capped by the four-thread ceiling, the presence of dedicated vCPUs eliminates neighbor contention. The bundled 400 GB NVMe tier avoids independent storage attach overhead, though write-heavy transactional databases may encounter performance limits during high-concurrency loads. The server aligns best with memory-intensive deployments such as Redis and in-memory key-value caches, intermediate data preprocessing, compilation pipelines, and dedicated background service workers.
description: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-400s-amd is a memory-focused instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz across two physical cores and four vCPUs, it features an x86_64 architecture with support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. The server is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-core ratio, alongside a bundled 400 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core compute capabilities and strong uncached memory write throughput exceeding 112 GB/sec, while overall multi-threaded processing and static web serving remain in average-to-low ranges. This density profile provides qualitative cost efficiency when RAM capacity requirements outweigh parallel CPU demand. The instance matches workloads such as in-memory caching layers, text extraction tasks, and memory-constrained application backends.
